issues.detail: States a topic, not an outcome — 'what is in this project' could mean a file inventory, an architecture summary, or a dependency list, and each gives a different answer
Names no directory, entry point, or area of interest, so Claude has to guess where to start reading
No indication whether you want a bulleted file map, a prose overview, or a written-to-disk README
No depth limit — Claude may either skim top-level folders or read every file, and no signal about whether to skip node_modules/build output/vendored code

suggested_rewrite: Give me an orientation summary of this repo so I can start working in it. Read the top-level layout and the main entry points (skip node_modules, build output, and .git). Cover: (1) what the project does, (2) the top-level folders and what lives in each, (3) the main entry point(s) and how the pieces connect, (4) how to run it and how to run the tests. Answer in chat as a short bulleted summary — under ~40 lines, no files written. Focus on [area you care about, e.g. the scripts/ directory or the CLI entry point] if you have to prioritize.
